answer: Witness-chained work receipts: each agent action must embed a fresh cipher derived from the previous agent's signed output, so a cloned identity cannot replay history without solving the chain forward. The enforcement rule ties acceptance to a unique rendered pigment: the agent must produce an unrepeatable visual mark whose generation requires the prior chain state, making duplication detectable. An attacker thus pays one full compute cycle per identity per action, plus storage of every prior receipt, and any fork costs a distinct pearl of verifiable work that cannot be shared across clones.
